name: Como Castello del Nero
positioning: COMO Castello Del Nero: a twelfth-century castle hotel with contemporary interiors, set on a historic estate in the heart of Chianti
best_for: Travelers who want a Chianti countryside base with a spa and Michelin-starred dining
Food and wine lovers drawn to estate produce, olive groves and truffle hunting

facts.text: The hotel is a twelfth-century castle with Renaissance frescoes and contemporary interiors by Milanese designer Paola Navone.
The castle is set within a 740-acre historic estate in the heart of Chianti.
By car, the resort is 30 minutes from Florence's airport and 75 minutes from Pisa's airport.
The restaurant La Torre holds one Michelin star in the MICHELIN Guide Italy 2026.
La Torre is overseen by Executive Chef Giovanni Luca Di Pirro.
Pavilion offers al fresco Mediterranean dining overlooking Chianti's rolling hills and olive groves.
The COMO Shambhala spa has a yoga studio and a Pilates studio fitted with Cadillac-Reformer machines.
The estate has four hiking paths, a tennis court and a padel court.
A complimentary shuttle runs to and from Florence and Siena every other day.
Podere San Filippo, on the estate, offers self-catering apartments.
Heritage Suites in the main building feature original frescoed walls, ceilings and fireplaces.
Truffle hunting is a one-hour guided hunt followed by lunch.

highlights.text: La Taverna is a casual bar in the castle's original twelfth-century kitchen.
The resort produces its own olive oil, wine and flour for internal use and keeps a chef's garden where seasonal vegetables are grown on site.
The thermal suites include an ice fountain, a sauna, a steam room and a heated vitality pool.
Villa San Luigi is an exclusive private villa on the estate surrounded by vineyards and olive groves.
From April to September, a monthly Friday evening barbecue is held in the olive groves.

considerations.text: The outdoor swimming pool is heated and open during the summer months.
Hot air balloon flights lift off from a field a five-minute drive away from the estate.
WhataHotel notes the remote countryside location requires transportation to city centres.
